req.title: Login required for delete
req.statement: The system shall redirect anonymous users to /auth/login when they POST /<id>/delete.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-014 requires that anonymous (unauthenticated) users who POST to /<id>/delete are redirected to /auth/login. Three test cases are designed: (1) positive — anonymous POST to a valid post id redirects to /auth/login with status 302; (2) negative — authenticated user POSTing to their own post's delete endpoint is NOT redirected to login (gets 302 to index instead), confirming the guard only fires for anonymous users; (3) boundary — anonymous POST to a non-existent post id still triggers the login_required decorator before any DB lookup, so the redirect to /auth/login still occurs (status 302, Location /auth/login). Each test uses exact status code and Location header assertions to kill comparison-operator and constant mutations.

tests.name: test_anonymous_post_delete_redirects_to_login
preconditions: Post id=1 exists in the database (author_id=5, user James)
actions: Create app with TESTING=True and a temp database
trace: R-FLASKR-014: anonymous POST /<id>/delete must redirect to /auth/login
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.post('/1/delete')
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login', f'Expected /auth/login, got {r.headers["Location"]}'
os.unlink(path)

trace: R-FLASKR-014: authenticated users must NOT be redirected to /auth/login on delete
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'James', 'password': 'river'})
assert login_r.status_code == 302, f'Login failed: {login_r.status_code}'
assert login_r.headers['Location'] == '/'

r = client.post('/1/delete')
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.headers['Location'] != '/auth/login', 'Authenticated user should not be sent to login'
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/', f'Expected /, got {r.headers["Location"]}'
os.unlink(path)

actions: Create app with TESTING=True and a temp database
GET to /1/delete (wrong HTTP method) without logging in

tests.name: test_anonymous_post_delete_location_exact_path
preconditions: Post id=2 exists in the database (author_id=1, user Rahul)
actions: Create app with TESTING=True and a temp database
Assert exact Location header value including path prefix
expected: Location header is exactly /auth/login (not /login, not /auth/login?next=..., not /)
trace: R-FLASKR-014: redirect target must be exactly /auth/login — catches constant mutations on url_for('auth.login')
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.post('/2/delete')
assert r.status_code == 302
location = r.headers['Location']
assert location == '/auth/login', f'Exact location mismatch: got {location!r}'
assert location != '/', 'Must not redirect to index'
assert location != '/login', 'Must use /auth/login not /login'
os.unlink(path)
